# Places to visit on the Wales Coast Path

There are lots of friendly, bustling towns along the Wales Coast Path. Here are some of our favourites where you can base yourself - complete with things to do, day-walks along the path, fine food and interesting detours.

## Whisky and waterfalls at Abergwyngregyn

Aber, for short, has a little buzz all of its own. It’s home of the [Aber Falls distillery](https://www.visitwales.com/product/2040971) and you can stop by for lunch. But take care – the visitor centre may tempt you to distil your own gin in their lab sessions! Or else try the delectable Welsh rarebit at [Caffi Hen Felin](https://www.facebook.com/caffihenfelin/?locale=en_GB). You'll find it in the village’s old mill, now a community centre.

The coast path here is gentle, running alongside the vast expanse of the Lavan sandflats that stretch almost to Anglesey, and are a birdwatcher’s paradise. For something a little different take a detour inland. A gentle and accessible meadow walk leads you to Aber Falls, the towering waterfall that gives the distillery its name.

Find out more about [walks around Abergwyngregyn](https://www.abergwyngregyn.org.uk/walks/).

## Tranquility and treasures at Beaumaris

Historic Biwmares (Beaumaris) might give you the shivers. You can follow the hair-raising 19th century judicial process from the [Beaumaris Courthouse](https://www.visitwales.com/product/912806) to [Beaumaris Gaol](https://www.visitwales.com/product/912808). And look out for the church clock, cursed by an inmate on the scaffold to be forever wrong! Moated [Beaumaris Castle](https://www.visitwales.com/product/2003622) is near perfectly symmetrical, with striking views from the turrets across the Menai Strait to Eryri (Snowdonia). There is peace for your soul here too.

You can find deep relaxation on an afternoon’s silk painting workshop at [H’artworks](https://www.hartworksgallery.co.uk/) or slip through the alleyway into the tranquil [Castle Gardens](https://www.facebook.com/Castle-Gardens-Beaumaris-503698233093348/). Boats leave from the pier for a gentle [cruise around Puffin Island](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1501902).

![castle and moat with tree.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimagegroup__landscape__2_1x/public/media-library/2025-04/733651-svw-h12-2526-0006-web-optimised-1920px.jpg.webp?itok=1ehzbKpC)

![Two cyclists watching yachts.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimagegroup__landscape__2_1x/public/media-library/2024-07/WCP_MG_9668.jpg.webp?itok=qYutLAfI)

Beaumaris Castle from above and views across the Menai Strait, North Wales

View Credits

It’s a steep climb south on the coast path but the views are tremendous - straight up the 140m (460ft) Allt Goch Bach on tree-tunnel back roads with glimpses back over the castle and Puffin Island beyond.

**Read more:** [Discover the Wales Coast Path](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3208)

## Heaps of creative energy at Caernarfon

There’s the towering drama of [Castell Caernarfon](https://www.visitwales.com/product/822841) here for starters, but once you've explored it, head for the [Galeri Caernarfon](https://www.visitwales.com/product/926139). It's very vibrant, and they’re involved in regenerating the harbourside with the [Cei Llechi](https://www.ceillechi.cymru/eng/home), arts and crafts workspace with markets and events. The annual [Gŵyl Fwyd Caernarfon Food Festival](https://gwylfwydcaernarfon.cymru/home.php) is an institution, and they hold events throughout the year. Even the airport has an [aviation museum](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1887769)!

![Castle in background with boats in foreground.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimagegroup__landscape__2_1x/public/media-library/2020-05/NCX-VH02-1819-0030-small.jpg.webp?itok=dkeZ0vXG)

![aerial view of food festival.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimagegroup__landscape__2_1x/public/media-library/2024-08/NVW-G33-2425-053.jpg.webp?itok=z5gjTC9B)

Castell Caernarfon's mighty towers overlook the River Seiont and Menai Strait and Gŵyl Fwyd Caernarfon Food Festival, North Wales

View Credits

© Hawlfraint y Goron / Crown Copyright

© Hawlfraint y Goron / Crown Copyright

For a mellow, eight-mile circular walk, cross the swing bridge and follow the coast path south out of town. Keep an eye out for 13th century St Baglan’s Church. At Saron, head east across fields to join [Lon Eifion](https://www.walkwheelcycletrust.org.uk/find-a-route-on-the-national-cycle-network/lon-las-menai-lon-eifion/), a walking route back to Caernarfon along a disused railway line. There’s also a stop for the plush [Welsh Highland Railway](https://www.visitwales.com/product/518186) here in case you’re ready for a lift.

![family cycling near railway station.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimagegroup__landscape__2_1x/public/media-library/2024-09/NVW-G47-2425-0077.jpg.webp?itok=p7Lo_k9p)

## Cosy hideaways at Y Borth

Y Borth is a friendly, arty little community, nestled behind the sea wall of the longest sandy beach in Ceredigion. There’s no shortage of characterful cafes to enjoy a brew and cake. There are galleries, craft and antique shops and the train station has a very sweet volunteer-run museum! Don’t miss [Libanus 1877](https://libanus1877.com/), named for the age of the chapel they’ve tastefully converted into a restaurant, bar and boutique cinema. Head to the [Friendship Inn](https://www.facebook.com/TheFriendshipInnBorth/) for a distinct chance of a locals’ singalong.

![Tree stumps on beach at sunset Submerged Forest.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_medium__4_3_1x/public/media-library/2025-06/47897-mvw-c60-0910-0097-web-optimised-1920px.jpg.webp?itok=zwG63F2k)

Sunset over the petrified tree stumps at Y Borth beach, Mid Wales

View Credits

© Hawlfraint y Goron / Crown Copyright

And [Borth beach](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1831066) is pretty epic! It’s golden, flat, perfect for kite sports and beginner surfing and famous for the 4500-year-old petrified tree stumps visible at low tide. The coast path heads inland here, an easy flat stroll alongside the peat bog with dramatic views of the hills either side of the estuary at the heart of the [UNESCO Biosphere](https://www.visitwales.com/node/5319). Look out for rare invertebrates and carnivorous plants!

**Read more:** [Discover the coastal communities of Wales](https://www.visitwales.com/node/2931)

## Estuary exploring at Solva

[Solfach](https://www.visitpembrokeshire.com/explore-pembrokeshire/beaches/solva-harbour) (Solva) is a pretty little harbour village in a sheltered inlet. Start by exploring the inlet on foot – the coast path goes right round, past the historic limekilns. At low tide you can walk down the estuary itself, out to a secluded cove. Or head up the hill to [Solva Woollen Mil](https://www.solvawoollenmill.co.uk/) l with working looms and turning water wheel. The [Raul Speek Gallery](https://raulspeek.co.uk/) is a Caribbean tonic for the soul. You might even meet Raul himself, painting or playing Cuban jazz. Try [Pointz Castle](https://www.facebook.com/pembrokeshireicecream/?locale=en_GB) for a tasty ice-cream or settle into the 16th century [Cambrian Inn](https://www.visitwales.com/product/930457) for a stylish meal.

For a good walk, you can head south on the coast path - four winding clifftop miles to the vast sands of Newgale Beach. Read more about the route on the [Pembrokeshire Coast website](https://www.pembrokeshirecoast.wales/coast-path/planning-your-walk/solva-to-broad-haven/).

![A harbour village surrounding a boat-filled estuary - houses one side, walkers on a path on the other.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_medium__16_9_1x/public/media-library/2022-12/SVW-E52-2223-0001.jpg.webp?itok=fWjc3t7t)

## Beaches and seafood at Saundersfoot

[Saundersfoot beach](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1443771) is the star of the show here. An immense sweep of south Pembrokeshire coastline. And the town has done a good job of providing places to eat whilst revelling in the sea view. Try [The Stone Crab](https://stonecrab.co.uk/) on the harbour – beautiful views while you gorge on oysters, crabs and lobsters. Fancy going upmarket a little? [Lan y Môr Restaurant](https://lanymorsaundersfoot.co.uk/) offers fine dining with floor-to-ceiling views of the sea at Coppet Hall.

![Boats in Saundersfoot harbour on a sunny day.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimagegroup__landscape__2_1x/public/media-library/2025-06/43352-saundersfoot-harbour-festival-pembrokeshire-fish-week-2017-web-optimised-1920px.jpg.webp?itok=s9qRAQrg)

![exterior of wood clad building with sign 'Lan y Môr' and outdoor seating.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimagegroup__landscape__2_1x/public/media-library/2024-08/WVW-G29-2425-0003.jpg.webp?itok=GsL8zXfG)

The harbour at Saundersfoot and nearby Lan y Môr restaurant, West Wales

View Credits

The coast path from Saundersfoot offers wheelchair/buggy/bike friendly wheeling on the [Dramway Trail](https://www.pembrokeshire.gov.uk/cycle-pembrokeshire/cycle-pembrokeshire-dramway-trail), including tunnels through the headlands at Coppet Hall and Wiseman’s Bridge. And what better place to end the day than in the infinity pool at the fancy [St Brides Spa](https://www.visitwales.com/product/221219)?

**Read more:** [Family cycling adventures on the Wales Coast Path](https://www.visitwales.com/node/5692)

## Cream tea at lively Llansteffan

When you’re finished at splendid [Castell Llansteffan](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1443734) high on the clifftop, head down to the friendly [Castle Inn](https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=100083538633322#) for some people-watching in the square, [The Inn at the Sticks](https://innatthesticks.com/) has music nights, or opt for a cream tea at the Beach Shop and Tea Rooms, with views across the Tywi to Ferryside. And if you’re up early, Jamie’s fresh bread from the [The Stores](https://www.facebook.com/jamiethebaker/) doesn’t wait around!

![The ruins of Castell Llansteffan from above, with the River Tywi estuary in the background.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_small__16_9_1x/public/media-library/2020-09/WCP_DJI_0594.jpg.webp?itok=GjpSq7Qy)

Views across Castell Llansteffan out across the Tywi estuary, West Wales

View Credits

© Hawlfraint y Goron / Crown Copyright

You can follow the coast path south around the shoreline to reach Scott’s Bay with its 19th century seaside villa here. Check out [St Anthony’s Well](https://coflein.gov.uk/en/sites/32259) as you pass – it has healing properties, they say. Turn back from here along the inland side of the castle. For a longer walk carry on along the coast path until you get to Wharley Point for views across [Carmarthen Bay](https://www.visitwales.com/product/2168928), all the way across to Devon. Check out the [Wales Coast Path website](https://www.walescoastpath.gov.uk/plan-your-visit/itineraries/cadw/llansteffan-circular-walks/?lang=en) for more walk information.

## Break for the border at Chepstow

Cas-gwent (Chepstow) is on the Welsh bank of the River Wye, laid out on the valley-side, perfect for wandering amongst the Georgian townhouses and independent boutiques. There are plenty of [things to do in Cas-gwent](https://www.visitwales.com/node/2957). One of the townhouses is the [Chepstow Museum](https://www.visitwales.com/product/914791), with tales of the town’s shipbuilding and wine-trading past. And visit the ancient [Chepstow Castle](https://www.visitwales.com/product/516062), of course!

![A view looking out at Chepstow Castle.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_medium__4_3_1x/public/media-library/2025-06/33559-chepstow-castle-monmouthshire-web-optimised-1920px.jpg.webp?itok=HoTbU3-5)

With its bridge and castle, Cas-gwent is right on the border with England

View Credits

© Hawlfraint y Goron / Crown Copyright

You're at the very end (or beginning) of the Wales Coast Path here, and long-distance walkers often link it up with the [Offa’s Dyke Path](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3306), that runs near-ish the full length of the border. Tempt yourself with its first five miles, north to Tyndyrn (Tintern), with the spectacular 12th century [Tintern Abbey](https://www.visitwales.com/product/527989) as your prize, especially viewed from the limestone outcrop, the [Devil’s Pulpit](https://www.visitmonmouthshire.com/things-to-do/devils-pulpit-viewpoint-p1504641). Then cross the river and come back on the Welsh side, via the [Wye Valley Walk](https://www.wyevalleywalk.org/) and its own lookout, the Eagle’s Nest. A challenging 14 mile-walk, but unforgettable!

**Read more:** [Luxury Wales Coast Path accommodation](https://www.visitwales.com/node/5680)
